analysis: The PR changes only documentation: one row added to a troubleshooting table in docs/architecture/inference.md (head line ~2371). It describes that a cold load can be refused with a 503 or an insufficient-memory error when an idle model slot holds an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. Held slots are excluded from eviction (ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel) and their weights receive no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit (autopilotHeldWeightBytes). No code, protocol, key handling, attestation, cache storage or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence. I checked the row against the threat model: it does not alter any cache, prefix-reuse or SSD behavior (T-041), the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053), or encryption boundaries. The row is an operator-facing availability explanation, and the documented hold-based refusal is a pre-existing behavior; this unit does not introduce it. I examined the base excerpt (lines 2398-2652) and the head excerpt (lines 1-415). Both are unchanged context apart from the patch hunk, and neither contains security-relevant drift. Remaining uncertainty: the referenced Autopilot source (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift) and model-autopilot.md are not in the supplied batch, so the accuracy of the described hold semantics, and whether holds could be abused by a consumer or provider for denial of service, is not verified. This is a code-level question for whichever pass covers those files, not a regression in this PR.
